findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the uploaded vendor roster) are stored without an enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 default encryption policy.
No ACL is specified and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so nothing prevents a later ACL or bucket policy from granting anonymous access to report data.
The bucket storing report data and the seeded vendor roster has no logging block, so access to sensitive objects cannot be attributed during an incident investigation.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial export data is stored without enforced server-side encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so a subsequent ACL or bucket policy change could expose ledger data publicly without any bucket-level guardrail.
No logging block is configured for the ledger bucket, leaving no audit trail of access to financial export data.
The model artifacts bucket configures versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored artifacts have no enforced default encryption.
No public access block resource constrains this bucket, so bucket ACLs or policies could later grant anonymous access to model artifacts.
Operational runbooks, which commonly contain internal procedures and sensitive system detail, are stored without any server-side encryption configuration.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against public ACLs or policies.
The runbooks bucket has no logging block, so access to its contents is not recorded for audit purposes.

The audit log destination bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block; combined with the log-delivery-write ACL (which grants the S3 log delivery group write access) there is no guardrail against a later policy or ACL exposing log data publicly.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket permits deletion of all log objects along with the bucket, undermining the integrity and non-repudiation of the audit trail.
The object is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument into a bucket with no default encryption, so the vendor roster file is stored without enforced encryption.
No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so objects can be read or written over cleartext HTTP.
No bucket policy enforces aws:SecureTransport, allowing ledger data to be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections.
No bucket policy denies non-HTTPS requests, so model artifacts can be transferred in cleartext over HTTP.
No bucket policy denies non-HTTPS requests to the runbooks bucket, permitting cleartext transmission of internal operational documentation.
The audit log bucket has no policy requiring aws:SecureTransport, so log data can be retrieved over unencrypted HTTP despite being encrypted at rest with KMS.

The ledger export bucket has no versioning block and force_destroy = true, so financial export objects can be silently overwritten or deleted with no recoverable prior version, weakening integrity and tamper evidence for financial records.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, so archived report objects can be overwritten or destroyed irrecoverably, defeating tamper resistance.
